When \(m=1\), \(\epsilon=1/4\), and \(b=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), the exact sharp interval is \([-1/3,1/3]\). The upper dual certificate is \(1-\frac43(q_{01}+q_{10})\), the lower certificate is \(\frac13-\frac43(q_{01}+q_{10})\), and each endpoint is attained by a mixing law with at most four atoms.

Let \(H_{m,\epsilon}:=\operatorname{conv}\{(g_m(q),f(q)):q\in K_{\epsilon}\}\). The set \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) is compact and equals
\[
 \left\{\left(\int g_m\,d\nu,\int f\,d\nu\right):
 \nu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\right\}.
\]
Every pair in \(H_{m,\epsilon}\) has a representing probability measure supported on at most \(N_m+1\) points of \(K_{\epsilon}\), and therefore has a compatible hierarchical SCM in \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) with at most \(N_m+1\) latent cluster laws. Consequently, for every \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), the sharp fiber \(\Theta_{m,\epsilon}(b)\) is a nonempty attained compact interval \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\), and each endpoint has a representing measure, and hence a compatible hierarchical SCM, supported on at most \(N_m={m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. If \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\), then \(D_m(b)=(L_m(b),U_m(b))\) with both dual extrema attained. If an optimal dual polynomial has contact image of affine dimension \(r\), its associated endpoint admits at most \(r+1\) atoms.

snapshot.stmt: Every \((\mu,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) has \(Q_i\sim\mu\), conditional count law \(C_i\mid Q_i=q\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}(m,q)\), marginal count law \(\Pr(C_i=c)=\int B_c^{(m)}(q)\,d\mu(q)\), and cluster-equally-weighted ATE \(\tau(\mu)=\int\{q_{11}/p(q)-q_{01}/(1-p(q))\}\,d\mu(q)=\int f\,d\mu\). Conversely, for every \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draw \(Q_i\sim\mu\); conditional on \(Q_i=q\), draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p(q))\) and conditionally treatment-independent binary potential outcomes \(Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1)\) with means \(q_{01}/(1-p(q))\) and \(q_{11}/p(q)\), respectively, independently over \(j\), and set \(Y_{ij}=A_{ij}Y_{ij}(1)+(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}(0)\). This construction belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}\) and has conditional cell probabilities \(\Pr((A_{ij},Y_{ij})=(a,y)\mid Q_i)=Q_{i,ay}\) almost surely.

defs.def:hierarchical-scm-class: \(\mathfrak M_{m,\epsilon}=\{(\mu,\mathcal M):\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon}),\ Q_i\sim\mu,\ (Q_i,(A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))_{j=1}^m)_{i=1}^n\text{ satisfies independent cluster sampling, conditional iid sampling, observed-cell calibration, latent ignorability, and consistency}\}\)

assumptions.ass:clusters-iid: \((Q_i,(A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))_{j=1}^m)\) are independent and identically distributed across \(i\).
assumptions.ass:conditional-iid-plate: Conditional on \(Q_i=q\), the vectors \((A_{ij},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))\) are identically distributed and mutually independent over \(j\).
assumptions.ass:observed-cell-calibration: \(\Pr((A_{ij},Y_{ij})=(a,y)\mid Q_i)=Q_{i,ay}\) almost surely for every \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\), \(1\le i\le n\), and \(1\le j\le m\).

For every finite \(m\ge1\) and every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(V_m\) is the restriction to \(K_{\epsilon}\) of polynomials of total degree at most \(m\) on the simplex, whereas \(f(q)=q_{11}/p(q)-q_{01}/(1-p(q))\) does not belong to \(V_m\).

For a continuous functional \(h:K_{\epsilon}\to\mathbb R\), \(\int h\,d\nu\) is identical for all \(\nu\in\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)\) and every feasible \(b\) if and only if \(h\in V_m\). For \(h=f\), universal point identification therefore fails for every finite \(m\), and every \(b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})\) satisfies \(L_m(b)<U_m(b)\).
For \(m\ge2\) and any \(q^*\in K_{\epsilon}\), the boundary moment vector \(b=g_m(q^*)\) has \(\mathcal F_{m,\epsilon}(b)=\{\delta_{q^*}\}\) and hence \(L_m(b)=U_m(b)=f(q^*)\).

For every \((\ell,u)\in\mathcal E_m\) and every \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\), \([L_m(b),U_m(b)]\subseteq[\ell^\top b,u^\top b]\). The lower equality \(L_m(b)=\ell^\top b\) holds if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_m(q):q\in K_{\epsilon},\ \ell(q)=f(q)\}\), and the upper equality \(U_m(b)=u^\top b\) holds if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_m(q):q\in K_{\epsilon},\ u(q)=f(q)\}\). For every finite \(m\geq1\) and every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(d_m(\epsilon)\) be the uniform approximation modulus in the preceding definition.  Then
\[
 \max_{b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}}\{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}
 =\sup_{b\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon})}\{U_m(b)-L_m(b)\}
 =2d_m(\epsilon),
\]
and
\[
 0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m.
\]
Consequently every feasible fiber has width at most \(2(1-2\epsilon)^m\).  For every \(0<\delta\leq2\), the integer plate-size condition
\[
 m\geq\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{-\log(1-2\epsilon)}
\]
guarantees \(U_m(b)-L_m(b)\leq\delta\) simultaneously for all \(b\in\mathcal B_{m,\epsilon}\).
